title: synchronize-credential-heartbeat-and-consolidate-async-stream-interfaces-across-sdks
author: Asha Mehta
description:
Motivation: several SDKs implemented lightweight token warmup / refresh in inconsistent ways (heartbeat vs periodic prefetch vs on-demand). That divergence caused production surprises when switching runtimes and resulted in duplicated logic in the platform tests. This PR standardizes a small, low-level "credential heartbeat" primitive across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and consolidates the async streaming consumer surface so cross-lang examples and docs match.

Summary of changes (single-line description of each logical chunk):
- Add CredentialHeartbeat primitive to each SDK: a tiny, battery-friendly keepalive that emits prefetch hints and exposes an optical TTL that integrators can query. The heartbeat intentionally does not perform token exchange — it calls the configured credential provider's prewarm hook.
- Unify streaming surface: normalize the async consumer contract (pull-style iterator + typed event envelope) and add lightweight StreamBuilder helpers for ergonomic composition. The surface keeps existing helpers but adds shims so old code continues to work with deprecation warnings.
- Add cross-SDK tests and examples demonstrating prewarm flow + graceful stream restart.
- Fix a flaky Go unit test by pinning a third-party timer mock and adding deterministic jitter in the heartbeat tests.

Why this approach: keep the primitive minimal (no hidden auth behavior), provide an explicit opt-in prewarm hook, and standardize the observable stream contract so docs, examples, and internal harnesses can rely on the same semantics across languages.

Migration notes:
- Existing apps using ad-hoc prefetch should only need to switch to the new prewarm hook name (see examples) or keep current behavior via compatibility shim. Deprecation warnings will surface for one release cycle.
- Stream consumer changes are additive: the StreamBuilder is optional. If you used earlier async helpers, they remain available but will log a migration hint.

Examples (illustrative):
Python:
from redwood_sdk import Client, CredentialHeartbeat
client = Client()
hb = CredentialHeartbeat(client.cred_provider, interval_seconds=45)
hb.start()  # non-blocking prewarm hint

TypeScript:
import { RedwoodClient, CredentialHeartbeat, StreamBuilder } from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new RedwoodClient()
const hb = new CredentialHeartbeat(client.credentials, { intervalSeconds: 45 })
hb.start()
const stream = new StreamBuilder(client).withModel('gpt-mini').build()
for await (const event of stream) { /* typed envelope */ }

Go (snippet):
hb := sdk.NewCredentialHeartbeat(cli.CredProvider(), sdk.HeartbeatOpts{Interval: 45 * time.Second})
go hb.Start(ctx)
stream := sdk.NewStreamBuilder(cli).Model("gpt-mini").Build()
for evt := range stream.Recv() { /* typed */ }

Checklist:
- [x] API design reviewed by SDK leads (Jon Park, Mei Chen)
- [x] End-to-end example in docs updated
- [x] Compatibility shims added (no forced breaking change)
- [x] Cross-language tests added to the integration matrix

CI notes: initial runs showed a flaky TestHeartbeatDeterminism in Go (dependency on third-party mock). I pinned the dependency and made the test deterministic by removing wall-clock reliance; CI re-run passed.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-8721, SDK-UI-311 (migration docs), SUP-4421 (incident reference)

Release notes (short): unify credential heartbeat primitive and add ergonomic StreamBuilder across SDKs; minor test and stability fixes.

release_notes: Standardize a minimal CredentialHeartbeat primitive (opt-in prewarm hook) and add ergonomic StreamBuilder/typed envelopes across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Backwards compatible shims included. CI flakes fixed for Go heartbeat tests.
notes_to_releaser: This release contains API additions but includes compatibility shims. Recommend advertising the new prewarm hook in migration docs and encourage teams to adopt the StreamBuilder for new code. No immediate infra rollout required.
testing_summary: Unit tests added in all SDKs + integration tests exercise cross-language prewarm and stream restart. Go flake was addressed. Local stress run: ~1k streams/min on the integration harness with heartbeat enabled.
changelog_entry: Added CredentialHeartbeat primitive and StreamBuilder helpers across SDKs; improved stream ergonomics and fixed Go test flake.
